data.name: MultiValuedBooleanRule

data.value: The '{0}' Connected System has no Connector Definition, so JIM cannot tell where it connects.

data.name: SecureEndpointConnectorUnavailable

data.name: ServerCertificateUnreachable
data.value: {0}:{1} could not be reached, so JIM could not read its certificate. This is a connectivity problem rather than a certificate one.

data.name: SettingNotFound
data.value: Setting with key '{0}' not found.

data.name: SettingReadOnly
data.value: Setting '{0}' is read-only and cannot be modified.

data.name: IdpThumbprintRequired
data.value: A thumbprint is required. JIM will not trust whatever the identity provider happens to be presenting.

data.name: IdpNotConfigured
data.value: No identity provider is configured (JIM_SSO_AUTHORITY).

data.name: IdpNoAnswer
data.value: no answer

data.name: IdpUnreachable
data.value: JIM could not reach the identity provider at {0}: {1}.
data.comment: {0} is a host name; {1} is the error, or "no answer".

data.name: IdpPlainHttp
data.value: The identity provider at {0} is reached over plain HTTP, so there is no certificate to check. Use HTTPS outside local development.

data.name: IdpConfigurationUnreadable
data.value: JIM reached {0} but could not read its OpenID Connect configuration: {1}.

data.name: IdpNameMismatch
data.value: {0}'s certificate was not issued for {0}. Trusting a certificate cannot fix this: the identity provider needs a certificate that names {0}, or JIM_SSO_AUTHORITY must use a name its certificate carries.

data.name: IdpUntrusted
data.value: JIM does not trust {0}'s certificate: its chain ends at "{1}", and nothing trusted for sign-in vouches for it. Trust that certificate authority for sign-in to enable sign-in.

data.name: IdpUntrustedIssuedBy
data.value: JIM does not trust {0}'s certificate: its chain ends at "{1}" (issued by "{2}"), and nothing trusted for sign-in vouches for it. Trust that certificate authority for sign-in to enable sign-in.

data.name: IdpNoTlsCertificate
data.value: JIM reached {0} but it presented no TLS certificate: {1}.

data.name: IdpTrustedConfigurationUnreadable
data.value: JIM trusts {0}'s certificate but could not read its OpenID Connect configuration: {1}. Check JIM_SSO_AUTHORITY.

data.name: IdpTrustedByOperatingSystem
data.value: {0}'s certificate is trusted by the operating system.

data.name: IdpTrustedByStore
data.value: {0}'s certificate is trusted through the JIM certificate store ({1}).

data.name: IdpNothingTrusted
data.value: Nothing was trusted. {0}

data.name: IdpNotPresenting
data.value: {0} is not presenting a certificate with that thumbprint now, so nothing was trusted. This is expected if its certificate was renewed since you looked; check its status again.

data.name: IdpAlreadyTrusted
data.value: '{0}' is already trusted for sign-in.

data.name: IdpWouldNotVouch
data.value: Trusting '{0}' would not make {1} trusted: a certificate in its chain has expired or is not valid. Nothing was trusted; the identity provider's certificate needs renewing.

data.name: IdpWidenedToSignIn
data.value: '{0}' was already trusted for Connectors and is now trusted for sign-in as well.

data.name: IdpNowTrusted
data.value: '{0}' is now trusted for sign-in.

data.name: ExampleAttributeOnType
data.comment: {0} is an attribute name; {1} the object type it belongs to. Used inside the expression messages below.

data.name: ExampleExpressionDoesNotParse
data.value: The expression for {0} does not parse: {1}
data.comment: {0} names the attribute and object type; {1} is the parser’s own explanation.

data.name: ExampleExpressionReadsConnectedSystem
data.value: The expression for {0} reads {1}, but Example Data creates Metaverse Objects and has no Connected System Object to read, so it never has a value. Read mv["..."] instead.
data.comment: {1} is the accessor the expression uses, such as cs["mail"]. mv["..."] is expression syntax and stays as it is.

data.name: ExampleExpressionReadsUngenerated
data.value: The expression for {0} reads mv["{1}"], which this template does not generate on '{2}', so it never has a value.

data.name: ExampleRefusalsJoined
data.comment: Joins two refusal sentences, in order.

data.name: PwdRequired
data.value: A password is required.

data.name: PwdNeverDisable
data.value: enableAccount accepts true, to enable the account as its password is set, or can be left out to leave the account's enabled state as it is. Setting a password never disables an account.
data.comment: enableAccount is the name of an API parameter and stays as it is.

data.name: PwdNeverExpiresNeedsAccounts
data.value: expiryBehavior NeverExpires needs the accounts to be named. A password set on every Connected System configured for Password Synchronization leaves "Password never expires" as each account has it; name the Connected System Objects to choose Never expires for them.
data.comment: expiryBehaviour and NeverExpires are an API parameter and its value and stay as they are.

data.name: PwdNoAccounts
data.value: At least one account is required. To set the password on every Connected System configured for Password Synchronisation, name no accounts at all.

data.name: PwdNotThisPersonsAccount
data.value: Connected System Object {0} is not one of this Metaverse Object's accounts.
data.comment: {0} is an id.

data.name: PwdSystemMissing
data.value: Connected System {0}, which holds Connected System Object {1}, does not exist.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are ids.

data.name: PwdConnectorCannotSet
data.value: Connected System Object {0} is in {1}, whose Connector cannot set passwords.
data.comment: {0} is an id; {1} is a Connected System name.

data.name: PwdTwoAccountsOneSystem
data.value: Connected System Objects {0} and {1} are both in {2}; a password can be set on one account per Connected System at a time.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are ids; {2} is a Connected System name.

data.name: MatchNoSource
data.value: An Object Matching Rule must have a source, a Connected System attribute or an expression, or it has nothing to match on.

data.name: MatchSeveralSources
data.value: An Object Matching Rule takes exactly one source, a Connected System attribute or an expression; this one has {0}. To match on a combination of attributes, write an expression that combines them.
data.comment: {0} is the number of sources.

data.name: MatchAttributeAndExpression
data.value: An Object Matching Rule's source is either a Connected System attribute or an expression, not both.

data.name: MatchNeitherAttributeNorExpression
data.value: An Object Matching Rule's source names neither a Connected System attribute nor an expression, so the rule has nothing to match on.

data.name: MatchNoTarget
data.value: An Object Matching Rule must name the Metaverse Attribute its source values are compared against.

data.name: MatchTargetTypeNotMatchable
data.value: The Metaverse Attribute '{0}' is {1}, which an Object Matching Rule cannot compare. Match on a {2} attribute.
data.comment: {1} is a data type name and {2} a list of data type names (Text, Number, LongNumber, Decimal or Guid), shown as the identifiers JIM uses.

data.name: MatchAttributeNamedNotOnType
data.value: The Connected System attribute '{0}' is not an attribute of '{1}', the Object Type this rule reads.

data.name: MatchAttributeIdNotOnType
data.value: The Connected System attribute with id {0} is not an attribute of '{1}', the Object Type this rule reads.

data.name: MatchAttributeTypeMismatch
data.value: The Connected System attribute '{0}' is {1} but the Metaverse Attribute '{2}' is {3}; an Object Matching Rule compares attributes of the same type. To compare them anyway, match on an expression that converts the value.
data.comment: {1} and {3} are data type names, shown as the identifiers JIM uses.

data.name: MatchExpressionTooLong
data.value: The expression is {0} characters long; an expression can be at most {1}.

data.name: MatchExpressionDoesNotParse
data.value: The expression does not parse: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the parser’s own explanation.

data.name: MatchExpressionReadsMetaverse
data.value: A matching expression reads only the Connected System Object, so it cannot read {0}: the Metaverse Object is what the rule is looking for. To compare with a normalised Metaverse value, derive a Metaverse attribute that holds it and match on that.
data.comment: {0} is the accessor the expression uses, such as mv["mail"].

data.name: MatchExpressionReadsNothing
data.value: The expression reads no Connected System attribute, so it would compute the same value for every object and match them all with the same identity. Read at least one attribute, as cs["attributeName"].
data.comment: cs["attributeName"] is expression syntax and stays as it is.

data.name: MatchExpressionUnknownAttribute
data.value: The expression reads {0}, but '{1}' has no attribute of that name.

data.name: MatchExpressionNonRepeatable
data.value: The expression calls {0}, which returns a different value each time it runs, so the same object would match a different identity, or none, on every synchronisation.
data.comment: {0} lists the function names.

data.name: LookupNoMatch
data.value: No Metaverse Object holds these values, so a synchronisation would try the next Object Matching Rule, and project the object if no rule matches and its Synchronisation Rule projects.

data.name: LookupAlreadyJoined
data.value: This object is already joined to {0}, the Metaverse Object it matches on {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a Metaverse Object; {1} is the value the match was made on.

data.name: LookupJoinedToAnother
data.value: The values match {0} on {1}, but another Connected System Object from this Connected System is already joined to it, so a synchronisation would record that this object could not join.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a Metaverse Object; {1} is the value the match was made on.

data.name: LookupWouldJoin
data.value: A synchronisation would join this object to {0}, matched on {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a Metaverse Object; {1} is the value the match was made on.

data.name: ProvSyncRuleUnavailable
data.value: Synchronisation Rule not available.

data.name: ProvAdvancedNotEvaluated
data.value: Advanced mapping, not evaluated here

data.name: ProvNoSource
data.value: No source configured

data.name: ProvHeldUnderAnotherType
data.value: Held as {0} until the next import: a schema refresh changed this attribute to {1}, so synchronisation leaves the Metaverse Object's value as it is until an import reads the attribute again.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are data type names, shown as the identifiers JIM uses.

data.name: ProvInputsHeld
data.value: Not evaluated: {0} until the next import, because a schema refresh changed its data type. Synchronisation leaves the Metaverse Object's value as it is until an import reads it again.
data.comment: {0} lists the inputs of the Expression that are affected.

data.name: ProvExpressionFailed
data.comment: The Expression engine’s own explanation of why it could not evaluate, shown as it is.

data.name: ProvValueNotConvertible
data.value: The Expression returned '{0}', which this {1} attribute cannot hold, so this source would supply no value and synchronisation reports an expression error.
data.comment: {1} is a data type name, shown as the identifier JIM uses.

data.name: ProvSeveralValues
data.value: The Expression returned {0} values, but this attribute is single-valued, so this source would supply no value and synchronisation reports an error.
